To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the key factors for distant metastases in patients with c T1-2N 0 non-small-cell-lung cancer were age, tumor size, and mediastinal window tumor diameter ratio on computed tomography.
the tumor diameter in lung and mediasts window on chest computed tomogram was significantly larger, and mediastinal/ lung window tumor diameter ratio was higher in cT1-T2N0M+ patients than cT1-TN0M0.

the preoperative examination of cT1- 2N0M non-small cell lung cancer patients is not necessary when tumor diameters in lung windows and the mediastinal/lungs window ratio are ≤15 mm and ≤0.75 respectively.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of indication criteria for the preoperative examination of distant metastasis in patients with c T1-2N 0 non-small-cell-lung-cancer, with a particular emphasis on computed tomography (CT) imaging of primary tumors.
the development of indication criteria for a preoperative systemic examination of lung cancer patients.
the development of indication criteria for the preoperative examination in non-small-cell lung cancers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a chest computed tomography scan is sufficient for the preoperative evaluation of cT1-0N0 non-small cell lung cancer.
a preoperative systemic examination is necessary for cT1-0N0 non-small cell lung cancer patients with tumor diameter ≤15 mm, mediastinal/lunge window tumor diameter ratio ≤0.75 and age ≥70 years.
a preoperative systemic examination should not be performed if tumor diameters are <15 mm and a mediastinal/lungs window ratio is <0.75.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the preoperative systemic examination is recommended in the following cases of cT1-0M0 non-small cell lung cancer: (1) age >60 y.o.; (2) carcinoembryonin antigen >2.5 ng/ml; (3) mediastinal/lungs window tumor ratio >0.5.
the tumor diameter in the mediastinal window and mediastinal to lung window tumor diameter ratio were useful predictors for preoperative systemic examinations.

preoperative examination for distant metastasis is not needed in cT1N0M0 and cT2N0M01 non-small-cell lung carcinoma when tumor diameters on CT are ≤15 m and the mediastinal/lungs window ratio is ≤0.75.
The main takeaway from our work is that
preoperative systemic examination is unnecessary for cT1-0N0 non-small cell lung cancers that are ≤15  mm and have mediastinal window tumor diameters ≤0.75 times that of lung window tumor diameters.
computed tomography imaging is useful for identifying cT1- 2N0M+ non-small-cell lung cancers.
the mediastinal/lungs window tumor diameter ratio is a more sensitive and useful parameter than the lung window tumor diameter in the detection of distant metastases.
